title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events

primary_sources.paraphrase: arXiv abstract (v1, 4 Nov 2026, cs.AI): a context-aware agent reads load history plus event text (notices, weather alerts, schedules), judges each event's relevance, timing and interactions, then forecasts the horizon whole or in segments drafted by sub-agents and reviewed by a main agent. Claims best results in most scenarios, without numbers. Links a code repository.

Full text: eight hourly load sets including PJM (test Jan 2025 to Jul 2026, 112 selected cases at 24 h, 28 at 96 h). Horizons 24 h and 96 h; metrics WAPE and NRMSE. A Qwen3.5-4B backbone trained by SFT then RL on four H100 GPUs. 14 baselines including Chronos-2, TimesFM-3, LightGBM and ARIMAX. No seeds, pre-registration or weights release stated.

Authors' repository: one commit, no licence shown. Agent runtime, inference, metrics and training entry points. The README says datasets, trained checkpoints and paper results are not bundled and the snapshot is not verified as the revision behind the paper's numbers. The demo runs on synthetic inputs with scripted replies and tests mechanics only.

claims.text: ElecLoad ranks first in 13 of the 22 metric comparisons in the main results table (second in six more).
claims.metric: first places out of 22 metric comparisons
claims.dataset: GEFCom2014, Nord, PJM, SPP, LCL, iFlex, AEMO, ERCOT
claims.baseline: 14 external methods including Chronos-2, TimesFM-3, LightGBM, ARIMAX

claims.text: On GEFCom2014 with constructed event effects, ElecLoad's 96-hour WAPE is 6.68% against 8.18% for MemCast, the next best method.
claims.dataset: GEFCom2014 load track with synthetic event effects, 200 test cases

claims.text: On the same GEFCom2014 cases, ElecLoad's NRMSE is 8.42% against 10.35% for MemCast.
claims.dataset: GEFCom2014 load track with synthetic event effects, 200 test cases

claims.text: On PJM day-ahead cases, ElecLoad's WAPE is 3.13%, against 3.43% for TimesFM-3, 3.61% for Chronos-2, 4.89% for LightGBM and 7.01% for ARIMAX.
claims.dataset: PJM hourly metered load, 112 selected test cases, Jan 2025 to Jul 2026

claims.text: On PJM 96-hour cases, ElecLoad's WAPE is 6.03%, against 6.11% for TimesFM-3, 6.90% for Chronos-2 and 7.07% for LightGBM.
claims.dataset: PJM hourly metered load, 28 selected test cases, Jan 2025 to Jul 2026

claims.text: Against its own direct-only variant on PJM, ElecLoad's paired WAPE difference is -0.35 points; the paper gives a 95% interval of -0.58 to -0.12 (no 90% interval).

claims.text: Removing event text raises ElecLoad's GEFCom2014 WAPE from 6.68% to 8.46%.

claims.text: ElecLoad uses about 18.7 thousand tokens per GEFCom2014 case, against 7.8 thousand for direct-only forecasting.

relevance.rationale: Hourly electric load, with PJM among the test sets (3). Horizons are 24 h and 96 h; nothing reaches our 168 h, so the day-ahead score applies (2). Weather is a known-future input: GEFCom2014 future temperatures are described as forecasts available at the origin, and for PJM weather enters as NWS alert text issued before the origin (3). The method's lever is event text, which our benchmark does not carry: our inputs are load history and a temperature series only, so the part of the claim that rests on notices and alerts has nothing to act on in our setup.

checks.notes: Central model: ElecLoad, a Qwen3.5-4B backbone fine-tuned by the authors (SFT then RL, DeepSeek teacher, four H100 GPUs). The trained checkpoint is not released: the repository README says checkpoints are not bundled and one search found none on Hugging Face, so there is no weights file date and training_overlap_risk is unknown. For reference only, the paper's PJM training origins end in Dec 2022, before our scored window. Pre-registration: none mentioned in the full text. Replication: one search found no third-party rerun, so unknown. Evidence strength is weak under spec.yaml: the code is public but the numbers cannot be reproduced from it (no checkpoint, no bundled data, snapshot not verified as the paper's revision, RL rollout and checkpoint selection not shipped), so these are in effect numbers without usable code. The PJM test span is long (about 563 days) but consists of 112 and 28 hand-selected cases chosen for entity, quarter and event-count coverage, not every origin. No seeds are reported; the only intervals are 95% paired intervals against the method's own direct-only variant, so ci90 is null. baseline_same_inputs is partly for external baselines: all run on the same cases, but each through its own input interface, so numeric models such as Chronos-2 and TimesFM-3 presumably did not see the event text; the inputs of ARIMAX and LightGBM are not stated. The headline GEFCom2014 result uses event effects the authors constructed, not real event records. The two foundation-model baselines sit close: on PJM 96 h TimesFM-3 is 0.08 WAPE points behind, with no interval given. Unverified: (1) which PJM series and zones are used (Data Miner 2 metered load and EIA-930 are both listed; whether JC or DOM appear is not known); (2) whether numeric weather covariates are given for PJM or only alert text; (3) Appendix C.5 beyond the three paired differences reported; (4) the repository's commit date and licence (none shown); (5) zhjai/ano-repo, seen in search only and not opened; (6) the paper's single-event and multi-event PJM case counts disagree between Appendix A.5 (33 and 28) and Table 9 (45 and 32). The pages were read through a summarising fetch, so table values are as that fetch reported them. Licence: no licence on the repository and no weights, so null; the paper text is CC BY 4.0.

label: PARTIAL
label_reason: The paper is a primary source on hourly electric load that includes PJM, but its central model is a fine-tuned 4B language-model agent with no released checkpoint, and the repository states it is not verified to reproduce the paper's numbers. The evidence is thin (selected test cases, no seeds, a synthetic-event headline, horizons of 24 h and 96 h) and the headline comparison cannot be re-measured with any model in runnable_models.
implementation_hint: Not runnable: ElecLoad is not in runnable_models, has no public weights, and training it needs the authors' SFT and RL pipeline on GPUs, outside the 60-minute CPU limit. It also needs event text (NWS alerts, PJM emergency notices) that our benchmark does not collect. Two of its baselines are ours or close: amazon/chronos-2 (models/chronos2.py) is on our leaderboard, and TimesFM 3.0 is a FoundationForecast wrapper (models_ff/run_ff.py), but they are not the headline claim.
